 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Brett Yormark will be moving on from his role as the Big 12 commissioner.
 The conference announced Friday that Yormark will leave to accept a new role outside of college sports in the near future. He's stepping down from his job as commissioner effective Jan. 31, 2027.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Yormark took over for Bob Bowslby after Oklahoma and Texas left for the SEC; he has been the Big 12 commissioner since Aug. 1, 2022. Yormark helped broker the conference's latest television deals and oversaw its expansion to include Arizona, Arizona State, BYU, Cincinnati, Houston, UCF, Utah and West Virginia — giving it a total of 16 teams.
 "Serving as the commissioner of the Big 12 conference has been an extraordinary honor," Yormark said. "I am looking forward to passing the baton to the next commissioner and continuing to cheer this league on as a lifelong fan of the Big 12."
 In addition to his efforts in conference and playoff expansion, Yormark helped the league sign a six-year TV contract extension with ESPN and Fox valued at $2.28 billion.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Leading up to the 2026 football season, he oversaw a multi-year agreement with Monster Energy, making the beverage brand the entitlement partner of Big 12 football and basketball regular seasons. As part of that deal, Big 12 football and basketball jerseys now feature a co-branded Monster Energy and Big 12 conference logo. That logo is also visible on fields and courts, and it can be seen across the conference's digital and social media channels, too.
 Plus, Yormark strived to make the Big 12 global. Each of the past two years, at least one Big 12 team has participated in Ireland's Aer Lingus College Football Classic. In 2025, that was Iowa State and Kansas State going head-to-head in Dublin. This year, TCU took on the ACC's North Carolina. Additionally this football season, Kansas and Arizona State faced off in a conference game at Wembley Stadium in London.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Yormark was CEO of Jay-Z's Roc Nation when he was hired to take over for Bowlsby in 2022.
 The conference will now have a void to fill in its leadership with the college sports landscape in unprecedented times due to College Football Playoff expansion, NIL, transfers, the potential passing of the Protect College Sports Act and more.
